**How one file works for both:**
- **Rust:** comments can be nested. The first line, `/* /* */`, opens two comment levels and closes only one. So Rust skips the whole C++ section until the `// */` line closes the second level, then compiles the Rust `main`. A `/*` near the end hides the closing `#endif`.
- **C++:** comments can't be nested, so the first line is just a finished comment and C++ compiles its own `main`. The Rust code sits inside `#if 0 … #endif`, so C++ never compiles it.

**Large N:** both versions add the numbers in chunks of 9 digits, so the answer is exact and doesn't overflow even for large N. If you don't give an N, the program uses 0.

The file has one leftover line, `// \`, that does nothing in either language. You can delete it.
